title: Ops-lean battle brief for account engineers (pilot-ready) - WIP
content:
Purpose:
Quick slide pack + speaker notes for Account Engineers to run 20–40 minute pilot-focused technical conversations. Emphasis: lean ops messaging, escalation-free canary checks, and immediate value levers (cache, routing, quantization). Target audience: SEs paired with AMs during onboarding and pilot phase.

Slide 1 — One-line opener
- Title: Pilot Checklist: Keep the App Live & Economical
- Speaker note: Start with a single sentence about what success looks like for the pilot: stable latency under X ms for 95% p50/p95, predictable cost per 1k tokens, no customer data leakage. Set the expectation up front.

Slide 2 — 3-minute risk map (talk track + triage knobs)
- Section: Common pilot failure modes (quick bullets): cold KV cache, bursty tails, model hallucination spikes, quota exhaustion, unexpected token inflation from user prompts.
- Triage knobs by priority: 1) routing policy (fallback to cheaper variant), 2) prefix/KV caching, 3) batch sizing ceiling, 4) quantization suggestion, 5) request throttling/backoff.
- Speaker note: Walk through a single example: chat app sees repeated 3–4 turn threads causing KV cache misses after model rollover — immediate fix: enable prefix cache + pin model variant for canary.

Slide 3 — Rapid objection responses (30s answers)
- Objection: "This will blow our spend."
  - Quick reply: "We recommend setting an initial per-route budget and enabling prefix caching + a 2-tier fallback to a smaller quantized variant. We can show a simulated spend delta in <10 minutes."
- Objection: "Latency is inconsistent at peak."
  - Quick reply: "We can pin a dedicated pool on the pilot or apply burst policies and a regional routing rule; also enable continuous batching with a small max wait to smooth tail latency."
- Objection: "We need private deployment for compliance."
  - Quick reply: "Private control plane option exists; for pilots we suggest a VPC-hosted sandbox to speed time-to-value then move to full Private if checklist passes."

Slide 4 — Quick play: 5-minute canary script (ops runbook)
- Steps:
  1) Create a pilot route with tags: environment=pilot, team=acct-xyz, budget=monthly-X.
  2) Configure routing policy: primary=model-A (gpu-opt), fallback=model-A-quant (quantized smaller).
  3) Enable prefix caching for top 20 prompt templates, set TTL=6h.
  4) Set batch size cap = 4 requests, max latency budget = 300ms for p95.
  5) Run smoke tests: 200 synthetic requests across 5 templates, capture p50/p95 and token-per-response.
- Speaker note: SEs should run steps 1–3 in console, then ask AM to apply budget constraint. Use provided smoke script (linked_artifact).

Slide 5 — Two quick examples to show impact (data to share fast)
- Example A: Customer X — enabling prefix cache dropped token usage by ~22% on Q&A flows; p95 latency improved 18%.
- Example B: Customer Y — introducing a quantized fallback cut cost-per-1k tokens by 40% in background tasks; user-facing model kept higher-quality variant.
- Speaker note: Keep numbers approximate and anecdotal; the goal is to give credibility and a next-step.

Slide 6 — Triaging quality regressions (mini decision tree)
- Is the regression prompt-specific? -> isolate with prompt set -> if yes, add prompt-based reranking or guardrail -> if no, check model version change -> rollback or A/B test.
- Quick rituals: daily eval set run for pilot, automated slack alert if top-10 prompts fall below threshold.

Slide 7 — SE checklist before handing to AM for pricing
- Confirm: stable p95 latency for at least 1 hour under 75th percentile traffic.
- Confirm: fallback route exercised in canary and doesn't degrade UX more than acceptable bound.
- Confirm: token-per-response averaged in expected band.
- Add: escalate if more than 3 incidents in 24 hrs.

Appendix A — Quick snippets for Slack and demo scripts
- Slack DM to AM: "Quick check: pilot route created for acct-XYZ (pilot). Prefetch cache + fallback quant variant enabled. Running smoke now — will post p50/p95 and token metrics in #pilot-results in 10m."
- Demo smoke command (example): run_smoke --route pilot-acct-xyz --templates common-qna --size 200 --report channel:#pilot-results

Appendix B — Links & artifacts to drop in the pilot email
- Link to prebuilt smoke script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/42
- Confluence playbook: CONFLUENCE-1234 /pages/ops/pilot-playbook
- Recommended email blurb for customer: short 3-line ask for test window and expected traffic patterns.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Collect 3 more crisp numbers for median pilot cost savings across verticals (sales asked for finance-backed numbers).
- Add a tiny visual for routing fallback path (one slide).
- Validate suggested default TTLs for prefix cache with infra team (Luca).

References and provenance
- Pulls together field notes from SE pilots in Q2–Q3 2025, recorded in #pilot-results and tickets JIRA-OP-879.
- Intended to be a compact deck to hand to AE+SE before the pilot kickoff.

End of pack — iterate and prune for a 6-slide public-facing version once we validate numbers.
